one_liner: Header-only AVX2 BGR-to-grayscale for 8-bit images; README claims roughly 3x faster than OpenCV cv::cvtColor.
what_it_does: RGB2Y<multithread, weighted>(image, width, height, stride, out) converts an interleaved 3-byte-per-pixel image to 8-bit gray, with OpenCV's 0.299/0.587/0.114 weights (weighted=true) or a plain average (weighted=false). Despite the name, the first byte of each pixel gets the blue weight, so it is BGR2GRAY on OpenCV's default layout (open issue #4). It takes raw pointers and an input stride counted in pixels, writes a packed width x height output, and so replaces cv::cvtColor(src, dst, COLOR_BGR2GRAY) only at the function level.
how_it_is_fast: Each step converts 10 pixels (30 bytes): two overlapping 16-byte loads widened to 16 bits, one _mm256_mulhrs_epi16 against a repeating B,G,R Q15 weight vector, packus back to bytes, then three pshufb masks gather each pixel's three products and saturating byte adds sum them, so no 32-bit dot products are needed. Rows are split across up to min(height/16, hardware_concurrency()) std::async tasks. The unweighted path sums channels in 16 bits and divides by 3 with mulhrs by 10923, which equals round(sum/3) for every possible sum.
when_to_use: BGR8 frames in OpenCV layout converted to gray on x86-64 with AVX2, where a 1-level difference from OpenCV on some colours is acceptable and an OpenCV dependency is not wanted.
Large frames processed multithreaded on machines with 16 or fewer hardware threads, where thread start-up is amortised and the row-split bug cannot trigger.
Equal-weight channel averaging (weighted=false), which is exact for all inputs.
As a compact example of pshufb-based deinterleaving of 3-channel pixels with AVX2.
when_not_to_use: When you need OpenCV's exact output: an exhaustive check of all 16,777,216 BGR triples against OpenCV 4.x's 15-bit BGR2GRAY formula gives 33.2% differing by one grey level (16.4% lower, 16.8% higher), never by more.
RGB-ordered, 4-channel, 16-bit or float input: weights are global constants in the header (swap B_WEIGHT and R_WEIGHT for RGB), and only 3-byte pixels are handled.
CPUs without AVX2 or non-x86 targets: the SSE path the README advertises was removed on 30 Sep 2018 (commit 6a822b7, open issue #5), and NO_AVX_PLEASE now does nothing.
Unpadded input buffers: the final 10-pixel block of the last row loads 31 bytes and reads 1 to 28 bytes past the end, depending on width mod 10.
Multithreaded calls on machines with 24 or more hardware threads: the row split overruns the image for some heights (see gotchas).

integration.dependencies: none for RGB2Y.h beyond the C++ standard library and <immintrin.h> (it uses std::vector and std::thread without including <vector> or <thread>); the main.cpp demo needs OpenCV 3.x for the CV_BGR2GRAY constant
integration.min_toolchain: Written for MSVC: it uses __forceinline, which g++ and clang++ on Linux do not predefine (checked with g++ 13.3 macro dump), and an unannotated switch fallthrough that -Wextra flags (-Wimplicit-fallthrough since GCC 7) under the Makefile's -Werror; Makefile otherwise asks for g++ -std=gnu++17 -mavx2 -march=native -Ofast
integration.platforms: x86-64 with AVX2 (also SSE4.1 _mm_extract_epi8); no SSE-only, NEON or scalar fast path
integration.thread_safety: Reentrant: no shared mutable state (per-call vector of futures; the weight vector is a per-translation-unit static const)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: raw-pointer API for 3-channel 8-bit BGR only, stride in pixels rather than bytes, packed output, and results differ from cv::cvtColor by one grey level on about a third of colours

gotchas: Out-of-bounds rows in the multithreaded split: thread_stride = ceil(height / threads) and threads-1 full chunks are launched before the remainder, and the final call always processes at least one row, so whenever (threads-1)*thread_stride > height the tasks read past the input and write past the output. Because threads is capped at height/16 this needs 18 or more hardware threads: a simulation finds 49 affected heights up to 4096 on 24 threads (for example 385 rows, 7 rows out of bounds), 225 on 32 threads (520 rows) and 1713 on 64 threads (721 rows: 28 out of bounds; 1000 rows: 38).

The input stride is in pixels (row i starts at data + 3*i*stride) while the output is written packed at out + i*width; RGB2Y_ref instead writes out[i*stride + j], so with padded rows the fast path and the reference disagree on output layout. Divide cv::Mat::step by 3, and only if it is a multiple of 3.
main.cpp's 'N pixels disagree' line compares RGB2Y with its own RGB2Y_ref, which reproduces the per-term rounding exactly (0 mismatches over all colours), not with OpenCV's output.
Each multithreaded call starts new tasks with std::async(std::launch::async); libstdc++ and libc++ create a thread per task (MSVC pools them), so small images pay thread start-up on every call.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: CompV (RGB24 to gray 449 ms vs OpenCV 3086 ms) and DeltaCV publish measured BGR/RGB-to-gray results against OpenCV, and H264Sharp measures cvtColor-style conversion by thread count; choose RGB2Y only when a single dependency-free AVX2 header for BGR8 to gray matters more than evidence, bit-exactness or maintenance.
verified_claims_summary: The only claim is the README's 'roughly 3x faster than OpenCV with AVX2, or 2x with SSE only', with no CPU, timings or OpenCV version; that sentence was already in the README at commit e67dffa (Feb 2017), when the kernel used 6-bit weights with truncation (up to 3 grey levels off OpenCV, 57.4% of colours different), and it was not re-measured after the 30 Sep 2018 rewrite to the current Q15 kernel, which also dropped the SSE path. main.cpp times both sides (50 warm-ups, 100 runs, RGB2Y multithreaded, OpenCV with its own parallel_for_) on the repo's test.jpg, but publishes no output; the only posted run (issue #1, OpenCV 3.4.3, a Debug build) had RGB2Y at 15139.5 us against OpenCV's 2592.71 us.
status_note: Abandoned: the kernel last changed on 30 Sep 2018 and the only later commit (23 Mar 2021) added the MIT license; four open issues (missing SSE path, BGR naming, an unexplained 'A bug?' report with an error image) have no replies. Vendorable after fixing the row split and padding the input.
